PF_STEPS|/coatThinF/overview: The pigmented, self-levelling epoxy floor coating {B351} is mixed 100 : 24 parts by weight for approx. 3 minutes at an ideal material temperature of +15 °C (pot life approx. 30 minutes), poured onto the sanded primer, spread with the notched trowel or the rubber squeegee in one pass at approx. 1 mm and rolled criss-cross with the spiked roller to release the air. Approx. 1.4 kg/m² per mm. The coating is kept free of damp for approx. 4–6 hours, walkable after approx. 12 hours, overcoated within 12–24 hours and fully resilient after approx. 7 days.
PF_STEPS|/coatThinF/points/0: approx. 70 N/mm² compressive, approx. 44 N/mm² flexural, Shore D approx. 72, Bfl-s1, ≥ 1.5 N/mm²
PF_STEPS|/coatThinF/points/1: resistant to oils, tyre softeners, dilute acids and alkalis and cleaning agents; standard RAL colours or transparent
PF_STEPS|/coatThinF/points/2: the spiked roller is run while the coating still flows: too late it leaves marks †
PF_STEPS|/coatThinF/points/3: batches are planned to the pot life so that every pass is joined wet in wet †
PF_STEPS|/coatThickF/short: {B351} with + 50 parts by weight of quartz sand Ø 0.1–0.6 mm (resin : sand 2 : 1), spread at approx. 2 mm — approx. 1.2 kg/m² {B351} + 0.6 kg/m² sand per mm; de-aerated with the spiked roller.
PF_STEPS|/coatThickF/overview: For high mechanical loads — forklifts, pallet trucks, impacts — {B351} is filled: after the components A and B have been mixed, 50 parts by weight of kiln-dried quartz sand Ø 0.1–0.6 mm are stirred in (resin : sand 2 : 1). The thick coat is spread with the trowel at approx. 2 mm — approx. 1.2 kg/m² of {B351} and 0.6 kg/m² of sand per mm — and rolled criss-cross with the spiked roller. The times are those of the thin coat: pot life approx. 30 minutes, walkable after approx. 12 hours, full resilience after approx. 7 days.
PF_STEPS|/coatThickF/points/0: the thick coat lies on the two-step sanded primer of {GBM} or on the sanded barrier primer
PF_STEPS|/coatThickF/points/1: the quartz sand is kiln-dried; damp sand foams the resin †
PF_STEPS|/coatThickF/points/2: where the slab is rough a scratch coat under the thick coat saves material
PF_STEPS|/coatThickF/points/3: the slip-resistant finish follows on the hardened thick coat
PF_STEPS|/slipF/short: An interspersing coat of {B351} (300–400 g/m²), quartz sand Ø 0.5–1.0 mm broadcast to excess (approx. 1.5 kg/m²), the loose sand removed after hardening, the top seal of {B351} rolled criss-cross (400–800 g/m²): R11, up to R12.
PF_STEPS|/slipF/overview: Where the floor is wet or oily in use the surface is made slip resistant: an interspersing coat of {B351} is rolled onto the hardened coating (approx. 300–400 g/m²), quartz sand Ø 0.5–1.0 mm is broadcast to excess while fresh (approx. 1.5 kg/m²), the loose sand is swept and vacuumed after hardening, and the top seal of {B351} is rolled criss-cross (approx. 400–800 g/m²). The floor reaches slip class R11 by test report, up to R12 depending on the sand and the seal. In the aqueous seals {ANTI} produces the slip resistance instead.
PF_STEPS|/slipF/points/0: the top seal is rolled thin and even: a thick seal fills the profile †
PF_STEPS|/slipF/points/1: a transparent top seal keeps the colour of the coating
PF_STEPS|/slipF/points/2: the cleaning of a profiled floor is planned with the scrubber-drier: the coarser the profile, the harder the cleaning †
PF_STEPS|/slipF/points/3: walkable after approx. 12 hours; full resilience after approx. 7 days
PF_STEPS|/vprimeF/short: {V360} mixed 100 : 20, diluted with 8–10 % water (max. 10 %), rolled criss-cross with the nylon fur roller, approx. 0.15 kg/m²; the seal after 16–48 hours.
PF_STEPS|/vprimeF/overview: The water-emulsified epoxy {V360} is its own primer: the component A is stirred, the component B added and both mixed for approx. 3 minutes (100 : 20 parts by weight, pot life approx. 40 minutes); 8–10 % water is stirred in (not more than 10 %) and the primer rolled criss-cross with the nylon fur roller onto the dry (≤ 5 CM-%), prepared substrate — concrete, cement and calcium sulphate screeds, magnesia screed, sanded mastic asphalt — approx. 0.15 kg/m². The seal follows after min. 16 hours and within 48 hours.
PF_STEPS|/vprimeF/points/0: substrate and air 10–35 °C, at least 3 °C above the dew point, relative humidity at most 65 %
PF_STEPS|/vprimeF/points/1: cracks are closed beforehand, e.g. with {GHS}
PF_STEPS|/vprimeF/points/3: the garage, the cellar, the warehouse: two days from the primer to the walkable floor
PF_STEPS|/vlevelF/short: Pinholes and recesses filled with {V360} + approx. 3 % {FF}; unevenness up to 2 mm levelled with {V360} + 50 % quartz sand Ø 0.1–0.35 mm; sanded with 100 grit and vacuumed after hardening.
PF_STEPS|/vlevelF/overview: Pinholes and small recesses are filled with {V360} thickened with approx. 3 % {FF}; unevenness up to 2 mm is levelled with a scratch coat of {V360} and quartz sand Ø 0.1–0.35 mm (resin mix : sand 1 : 0.5 by weight). After hardening the levelling is sanded with 100 grit and vacuumed, and the seal follows within the overcoat window of 16–48 hours — beyond it the surface is sanded again.
PF_STEPS|/vlevelF/points/0: approx. 1.6 kg/m² per mm of the levelling
PF_STEPS|/vlevelF/points/1: the levelling is thin: the aqueous system is a seal, not a floor screed
PF_STEPS|/vlevelF/points/2: a smooth, closed surface shows every pinhole under the satin seal — the levelling is worth the hour †
PF_STEPS|/vsealF/short: {V360} rolled criss-cross in one to two steps, approx. 0.30–0.35 kg/m² per step: pigmented, satin, vapour permeable; resistant to tyre softeners, dilute acids and alkalis, heating oil and petrol; walkable after 16 hours.
PF_STEPS|/vsealF/overview: The seal is mixed like the primer, undiluted, and rolled criss-cross with the nylon fur roller in one to two steps, approx. 0.30–0.35 kg/m² per step; the second step after min. 16 hours and within 48 hours. The hardened seal is pigmented in the standard RAL colours (approx. 7032, 7030, 7035, 1001, 7040), satin and vapour permeable, so that the slab can still breathe; it resists the softeners of car tyres, dilute acids and alkalis, heating oil and petrol. Walkable after approx. 16 hours, full resilience after approx. 7 days.
PF_STEPS|/vsealF/points/0: {ANTI} at 8–10 % by weight in the last step for slip class R10
PF_STEPS|/vsealF/points/1: approx. 1.4 g/cm³ ready to use; approx. 2,800 mPa·s
PF_STEPS|/vsealF/points/2: the garage floor is driven on after 7 days; tyres are not turned on the spot in the first weeks †
PF_STEPS|/vsealF/points/3: the wall–floor joint is closed with {IPU}
PF_STEPS|/antiF/short: {ANTI}, the spherical glass granulate of 90–150 µm, stirred into the premixed seal at 8–10 % by weight (max. 170 g/m² in the sealing layer): R10 with {V360}, R11 with {V2260}.
PF_STEPS|/antiF/overview: For a slip-resistant aqueous seal the ready-to-use glass granulate {ANTI} is stirred into the premixed, low-viscosity seal at approx. 8–10 % by weight — not more than 170 g/m² in the sealing layer — and the seal is rolled as usual. The granulate is stirred up during the work so that it does not settle in the bucket. By test report the floor reaches R10 with {V360} and R11 with {V2260}.
PF_STEPS|/antiF/points/0: grain size > 90 to 150 µm, bulk density approx. 1.35 g/cm³, transparent / matt
PF_STEPS|/antiF/points/1: the slip-resistant seal with {V2260}: approx. 120 g/m²
PF_STEPS|/antiF/points/2: the granulate goes into the last step only; the primer and the first step stay smooth
PF_STEPS|/antiF/points/3: stored cool and dry; minimum 36 months
PF_STEPS|/puF/short: {V2260}, the aqueous two-component PU seal, mixed 100 : 20 with approx. 5 % water, rolled in one step on the cured coating, approx. 80–150 g/m²: transparent, glossy, light-fast, UV-stable, scratch resistant.
PF_STEPS|/puF/overview: The showroom and the workshop get the glossy, easy-to-clean finish: {V2260} is mixed 100 : 20 parts by weight with approx. 5 % water for approx. 3 minutes and left to mature for approx. 2 minutes (pot life approx. 25–35 minutes at 10–30 °C), then rolled thin and even in one step with the nylon fur roller onto the cured, clean coating — approx. 80–150 g/m². The transparent seal is glossy, light-fast and UV-stable, scratch and abrasion resistant, with good migration resistance; EMICODE EC 1PLUS. Full resilience after approx. 7 days.
PF_STEPS|/puF/points/0: substrate 10–30 °C, dry (≤ 4 CM-%), at least 3 °C above the dew point
PF_STEPS|/puF/points/1: overcoat windows by temperature: +30 °C 2–3 to 12 hours; +20 °C 4–15 to 24 hours; +10 °C 9–13 to 48 hours
PF_STEPS|/v2370F/title: Coat the sewage structure with ASODUR-V2370
PF_STEPS|/v2370F/short: {V2370} mixed 7 : 1, two layers in alternating colours on the primed concrete (approx. 400–500 g/m² per layer); on steel blasted to Sa 2½ the first layer is the primer; XWW4, sulphuric acid pH 0–1.
PF_STEPS|/v2370F/overview: On the cementitious substrate primed with {SG3T} — and directly on steel blasted to Sa 2½ (DIN 55982), where the first layer acts as the primer — the sealing coating {V2370} is applied in two layers: mixed 7 : 1 parts by weight for approx. 3 minutes, rolled or sprayed at approx. 400–500 g/m² per layer on concrete, the second layer in the alternating colour (pebble grey, red, black) so that the coverage shows. The pot life follows the temperature (approx. 90–110 minutes at +10 °C, 45–55 at +20 °C, 22–28 at +30 °C), as do the overcoat windows (+10 °C: 24–36 to 48 hours; +20 °C: 12–16 to 24 hours; +30 °C: 6–8 to 12 hours) and the full resilience (10, 7 or 3 days). The coating is elastifying (Shore A approx. 80), stray-current insulating and resistant to sewage, sea water and sulphuric acid down to pH 0–1 — exposure class XWW4 after DIN 19753.
PF_STEPS|/v2370F/points/0: substrate 10–30 °C, dry (≤ 6 CM-%), at least 3 °C above the dew point, relative humidity at most 80 %
PF_STEPS|/v2370F/points/1: the chemical resistance table of the data sheet rates petrol, heating oil, alcohols, esters, formaldehyde, acetic acid, sulphuric acid 20 %, amines, surfactants and de-icing salt for 8 hours, 72 hours and 14 days
PF_STEPS|/v2370F/points/2: the coating is protected from moisture until it has hardened
PF_STEPS|/v2370F/points/3: breakouts and gullies are grouted with {EV200} before the coating; the movement joints are filled with {IPU}
PF_STEPS|/jointF/short: Field, connection and wall joints 10–30 mm wide, depth after width : depth 1 : 0.8, backed with a closed-cell cord, primed and filled with {IPU}; edges chamfered 45° under vehicle traffic; approx. 100 ml/m at 10 × 8 mm … 750 ml/m at 30 × 24 mm.
PF_STEPS|/jointF/overview: The field joints, connection joints and wall joints of the floor are taken through the coating and filled elastic: the joint 10–30 mm wide, the depth after the rule width : depth 1 : 0.8 (e.g. 15 × 12 mm, 20 × 16 mm), set with a closed-cell, rot-resistant backing cord approx. 20 % wider than the joint, the flanks primed (e.g. {SG3F}, approx. 200 g/m² absorbent, 150 g/m² non-absorbent, the joint filled after 3.5–48 hours) and filled with the one-component, moisture-curing polyurethane {IPU}, pressed against the flanks and smoothed. On components with vehicle traffic the edges are chamfered 45° (approx. 5 mm); the chamfer is not filled.
PF_STEPS|/jointF/points/0: Shore A approx. 40, recovery > 90 %, permissible total deformation 25 %, service temperature −40 to +80 °C
PF_STEPS|/jointF/points/1: skin formation after 60–90 minutes; 80 % of the final Shore A after 2 days at +23 °C; full loadability after 14 days at approx. +20 °C
PF_STEPS|/jointF/points/2: substrate and air approx. 5–40 °C, at least 3 °C above the dew point
PF_STEPS|/jointF/points/3: consumption: approx. 100 ml/m at 10 × 8 mm, 180 at 15 × 12, 320 at 20 × 16, 500 at 25 × 20, 750 at 30 × 24 mm
PF_STEPS|/jointF/points/4: a movement joint is not coated over: a coating bridges a joint only until the slab moves †
PF_STEPS|/cureF/short: Kept free of damp for 4–6 hours, walkable after approx. 12 hours (16 hours for {V360}), fully resilient after approx. 7 days; joints loadable after 14 days; protected from traffic until then.
PF_STEPS|/cureF/overview: The resins cure by reaction, not by drying: the fresh layers are protected from moisture for approx. 4–6 hours (contact with water leaves white marks and a weak surface), the floor is walked only after approx. 12 hours ({V360}: 16 hours; the non-sanded barrier primer only with clean overshoes), and it carries its full load — the forklift, the car, the chemicals — after approx. 7 days ({V2370}: 10, 7 or 3 days by temperature). The joints of {IPU} reach their full loadability after 14 days. In the meantime the floor is kept closed to other trades or protected with boards †.
PF_STEPS|/cureF/points/0: the curing follows the temperature: cold slows it, warm shortens the pot life
PF_STEPS|/cureF/points/1: the overcoat windows are kept: a layer that has waited too long is sanded before the next
PF_STEPS|/cureF/points/2: the first cleaning only after full resilience, with the cleaning agent of the data sheet ({R008})
PF_STEPS|/cureF/points/3: keep damp off for approx. 4–6 hours ({GBM}, {B351})
PF_STEPS|/serviceF/short: Closed, seamless, easy to clean: oil, tyre softeners, cleaning agents and dilute acids stay on the surface; the forklift meets 70 N/mm²; the joints move; the floor is cleaned with {R008} and re-sealed when it wears.
PF_STEPS|/serviceF/overview: The finished floor is closed and seamless: the primer has sealed the pores of the concrete, the coating carries the load (approx. 70 N/mm² compressive, Shore D approx. 72 for {B351}; approx. 109 N/mm² for the grouted bases), the seal takes the chemicals — oils, tyre softeners, cleaning agents, dilute acids and alkalis; {V2370} the sewage and the sulphuric acid — and the elastic joints follow the movement of the slab. Dust is gone, spills are wiped up, the floor is cleaned with the scrubber-drier and {R008}. When the top seal wears after years of traffic it is sanded and re-sealed: the system is renewed from the top, not replaced.
PF_STEPS|/serviceF/points/0: the barrier primers keep working underneath: vapour and oil stay in the slab
PF_STEPS|/serviceF/points/1: the slip class is kept by the cleaning: a floor coated with dirt and oil is slippery whatever its profile †
PF_STEPS|/serviceF/points/2: inspection of the joints and the edges with the annual cleaning †
PF_STEPS|/serviceF/points/3: a floor coating is wear protection: it is renewed from the top
PF_STEPS|/notesF/title: Observe the limits of the data sheets
PF_STEPS|/notesF/short: Substrate and air 10–35 °C (10–30 °C for {V2260}, {V2370}), at least 3 °C above the dew point, relative humidity at most 80 % (65 % for {V360}); pot lives and overcoat windows; storage frost-free; safety data sheets.
